messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: elevated DNS resolution failures for EU ingress (eu.app.redwood.ai) and increased 5xxs for EU traffic. Pager: @sara_sre. Event=DNS-EU-1998. 09:04 UTC.

sara_sre: I'm on call. Initial checks: lots of NX/TCP-truncation + SERVFAIL from several public resolvers (1.1.1.1, 8.8.4.4) when querying CF-proxied hostnames. Route53 authoritative NS answers look normal.

kenny_platform: Confirmed from our synthetic probes: UDP responses often truncated (TC=1) which forces TCP; many clients/timeouts follow. Example: `dig @1.1.1.1 eu.app.redwood.ai A +dnssec` -> Truncated.

dan_cloudops: Traceroutes to CF recursives show packet loss in eu-west-1 ISP fabric. Could be regional CF recursive issue or middlebox dropping TCP DNS. Opened quick check with Cloudflare support.

emma_cs: Customers: two enterprise customers in EU have active incidents — webhooks failing, auth handshakes dropping. CS escalations in progress.

sara_sre: Short terms mitigations: 1) create origin-only hostnames (no CF proxy, authoritative Route53) for control-plane and critical webhook endpoints 2) set region-specific geo records to prefer Route53 answers in EU 3) reduce TTLs to 20s on those records. Doing (1) -> (3) in that order.

deploy-bot: runbook:origin-hosts initiated by sara_sre at 09:08 UTC.

kenny_platform: Command to add origin record (Route53):
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZXYZ --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"webhooks-origin.eu.app.redwood.ai","Type":"A","TTL":20,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"35.158.10.21"}]}}]}'
```

sara_sre: After upserting origin A, switched the control-plane CNAME to point to webhooks-origin for critical names. Quick queries from 8.8.8.8 resolved to origin IPs within ~40s. Control-plane/keystone auth restored.

dan_cloudops: Next step: update GDNS policy to prefer route53-origin for geo region eu. Running gdns api call to flip weights.

deploy-bot: gdns-change executed by sara_sre at 09:11 UTC 4ms. New weights pushed.

cf-bot: Cloudflare ticket #CF-928312 opened (link posted), engineering investigating recursive resolver behavior in EU. Current status: Investigating.

emma_cs: Sent customer ACK at 09:13 UTC to affected accounts: "We're aware of DNS resolution errors in EU causing intermittent failures. Engineers applied temporary origin routing; monitoring. Will follow up with postmortem."

sara_sre: Lowered TTLs to 20s for impacted records and control-plane names to accelerate client updates. Note: this will spike authoritative QPS for Route53 10x expected. Monitoring route53 quotas.

kenny_platform: Observing resolver success rate improve for origin-hosted names but some clients still hitting CF-proxied name that returns truncated responses. We'll keep origin fallback until CF confirms resolution.

dan_cloudops: Collected dnslog samples and pcap of queries -> showing TCP retries and timeouts to CF recursive IP ranges. Storing artifacts in incident ticket INC-1998887776 artifacts folder.

sara_sre: Metrics: EU 5xx rate fell from 7.5% -> 0.8% within 12 minutes after origin routing. Webhook success rate for affected customers returned to normal.

emma_cs: Customer update at 09:30 UTC: "Mitigation applied; services restored for most customers. We're monitoring."

cf-bot: Cloudflare update: "We are investigating recursive resolver anomalies in EU; mitigations being applied to routing. We will provide updates." Link: https://status.cloudflare.com/incident/CF-REC-EU-1998

kenny_platform: Note for post-incident: CF-proxyed zones may trigger larger UDP responses (EDNS0 options) -> higher truncation risk. Control-plane records should avoid CF proxy or enable smaller responses.

dan_cloudops: Handoff: sara_sre -> dan_cloudops at 09:35 UTC for post-incident follow-up and postmortem. Sara offcall at 09:40 UTC.

sara_sre: My final: documented all Route53 change-ids, runbook commands, and CF ticket number in INC-1998887776. Leaving the geo-fallback in place for 60 minutes then reevaluate.

emma_cs: Sent final customer message at 09:50 UTC: "Incident mitigated: DNS resolver issues in EU impacted service; temporary origin routing applied. No data loss. Postmortem to follow."

dan_cloudops: Creating postmortem PM-1998887776; action items: automated geo-fallback when X% of regional DNS probes show truncation/SERVFAIL; add synthetic UDP/TCP DNS tests across CF recursive nodes; document recommended non-proxy hostnames for control-plane.

kenny_platform: We'll also add an alert in prod-monitoring for sudden increase in TC=1/TC=0 ratio and for difference between authoritative vs recursive responses.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated at 09:58 UTC; active monitoring. Next steps: postmortem due in 72h."
